Manx: Ta’n bundeil cummal ny pabyryn as ny “Sharmaneyn” er roshtyn, as te mee feer, feer, booisal diu er nyn son —
English: The bundle containing the papers and the “Sermons” has arrived, and I am very, very, grateful to you for them —

Manx: Ta mee hannah er chur shilley siyragh harrish ny arraneyn, agh cha leah as vees caa aym, jeeaghyn harrystoo reesht ny s’kiaralagh, roish my verym back ad —
English: I have already had put hurried sight over the songs, but as soon as I have a chance, to look over them again carefully, before I send them back —

Manx: Nee’m cur scrieunyn ny s’lhiurey hiu mychione ny reddyn shoh kione ghaa ny three sy laghyn —
English: I’ll send you longer letters about these things in two or three days —

Manx: Ta mee yeearree dy chyndaa hood my wooise son y pabyr naightagh, “Figaro”, as myrgeddin son y liooar beg bwaagh scrieut liort hene, hug shiu hym tammylt beg er-dy-henney —
English: I want to return my thanks for the news paper “Figaro”, and also for the little book written by yourself, that you sent me a little while ago —

Manx: T’eh lickly nagh vel shiu er ny gheddyn lioar Dr Leo dou foast? Veign feer bwooiagh er, my oddin y gheddyn eh [eh y gheddyn]
English: It’s probable that you haven’t found Dr Leo’s book yet? I would be very thankful for it, if I could get it

Manx: Neem cur hood screeunyn ny s’lhiuirey ayns traa gherrid —
English: I’ll send you longer letters in a short while.
